cost_planning_state: Dry run and tool qualification completed on the 30-item draft: 2700 normal / 5400 maximum HTTP measurement slots; 180 normal / 360 maximum HTTP preflight slots. Model difficulty preflight and registration are still pending. Earlier partial preflight campaigns are retained but not resumed; a fresh full preflight precedes registration.
cost_basis: The largest initial serialized message is 10739 bytes before request metadata. Plan conservatively at 20000 input tokens and 16384 output tokens per attempt, using the observed 2026-10-08 endpoint maxima USD0.45/2.40 per million for DeepSeek and USD0.17/0.25 for Qwen. All slots plus retries estimate USD150.70752 measurement and USD10.047168 preflight; round to caps160 and12. Feedback or provider prices can exceed these estimates. The enforced rule is reported-cost stopping, not a hard invoice ceiling. Replacements consume only the remaining total preflight allowance.
cost_stop: The caps apply to reported cost, not an absolute provider invoice. Bill both attempts. Do not start another attempt after the cap. Unknown usage is null, not zero. Amended before registration: an attempt with unknown usage no longer stops the campaign. It adds unknown_cost_reserve_usd, the rounded DeepSeek planning maximum per attempt, to the amount compared with the cap; its per-request cost stays null and the receipt counts these attempts. With parallel slots, every attempt already in flight can cross the cap. An HTTP 401 or 402 refusal stops the campaign; the provider key has its own USD 10 spending limit.
preflight_continuation: Owner-approved before registration: resume only the unattempted suffix in a fresh output directory. Preserve every old row, transcript, reported cost and prior receipt; do not reset failed/error slots or add retries. Require the same plan, order, corpus, prompt, predictions, models, compilers and sealed image. Only the reviewed harness/protocol amendment may differ, with both provenances retained. After an unknown-cost stop, first review aggregate key usage and retain a conservative allowance for previous unitemized charges; these charges stay null in per-request records. Future unknown usage still stops the continuation. The total preflight allowance does not reset.
fresh_preflight: At 2026-10-08T13:54:29Z the key reports USD0.122263969 daily and USD0.320553001 lifetime. Earlier experiment-2 preflight campaigns reported USD0.00309618 and USD0.0995587448. The fresh full preflight uses a USD10.90 reported-cost cap: USD12 minus the USD1 reserve for unitemized charges minus USD0.10265 reported earlier.
continuation_cost_review: At 2026-10-08T12:54:09Z the key reports USD0.049194125 daily and USD0.247483157 lifetime, unchanged since 12:04:16Z. These are aggregate amounts, not reconstructed per-request costs. Keep the USD1 reserve against the USD12 total allowance and the current campaign's USD11 reported-cost cap; also carry its USD0.03732025 already reported cost. This is conservative reported-cost accounting, not an absolute invoice guarantee.
http_retries: Each logical response slot has at most two HTTP attempts with the identical payload. Each attempt has a total wall-clock deadline of limits.http_timeout_seconds; OpenRouter keep-alive whitespace does not extend it. A timed-out attempt is a response error with unknown usage. Retry response errors once, including output exhaustion, malformed response and transport failure. Retry requests are additional to the 2700 normal slots and are fully billed. Do not layer the v1 HTTP retry loop underneath this rule.

conditions.c0: Only the current program and the registered C0 sentence. No tool output, score output or hidden information.
conditions.c1: Sealed gcc-14 -Wall -Wextra -fsanitize=undefined -o prog program.c, then ./prog. Return compiler stderr, runtime stderr and exit codes, as in the first study.
conditions.c2: Sealed clang-19 -Weverything -fsanitize=undefined -o prog program.c, then ./prog. Return compiler stderr, runtime stderr and exit codes, as in the first study.
conditions.c3: Host evo check --json; evo explain CODE --json for each reported code; evo fix --plan --json. Preserve all JSON records.
conditions.c4: Apply only evo fix --apply safe repairs to a disposable copy before feedback. Supply the actual edited source and applied diff, followed by C3 feedback. Record applied repairs, not available plans. Score a changed initial source before any model call; a success then uses zero model tokens. Repeat this process after each model response.

preflight: Before the tag, each item and each model gets three C0 first-response trials, one round each and one retry per response error. An item is hard for a model when at least two return valid candidates that fail hidden scoring; otherwise it is easy for that model. The harness records the hard items per model; predictions-2.md records the population decision before the tag. A response_error in the other trial is permitted, but contributes no failure or difficulty evidence. This restores the owner's two-of-three rule; the earlier draft's all-three-valid requirement was an extra restriction. Retain rejected drafts and preflight outcomes. Do not change an accepted item to improve measured outcomes. The USD 12 preflight allowance is a total across draft versions, not a fresh allowance per replacement campaign.
scoring: Sealed gcc-14 -O0 compiles the candidate with main renamed to program_main; the hidden reference calls at least ten distinct input sets and program_main. Pass requires exit zero and exact expected stdout. Hidden source, minimal repairs, spans and score details never enter model feedback.
round_stop: Stop at the first hidden pass or three logical response rounds. Two response failures end the repetition as response_error. Do not rerun failed measured repetitions. A partial or stopped population remains partial.
ordering: For each repetition, visit sorted item names, then the registered models. Rotate condition order by (item_index + repetition - 1) modulo the number of conditions. With --parallel N, slots start in this registered order under one lock and at most N run at once; each slot stays sequential inside. Each row records its start order and start time.
candidate_profile: One fenced complete C file, at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes, no external dependencies or I/O. Reject preprocessor markers after line-splice normalization. The same profile applies to all conditions; invalid responses consume their billed retry allowance.
isolation: Use the unchanged first-study candidate isolation: network-disabled ARM64 containers with no credential environment; candidate mounted read-only; hidden reference introduced only after candidate compilation and erased before execution.
http_deadline_basis: The earlier campaigns sent about 3.7 keep-alive bytes per second before each body. By that count, the slowest finished HTTP response took about 175 s (16384 output tokens) and stalled attempts ran about 14 minutes. A 300 s total deadline per attempt keeps every observed finished response.

metrics.repair_rate: Passes / (attempts minus response_error). Other errors remain in this denominator. Also report passes / all attempts as completion rate, response errors, other errors and unattempted cells separately.
metrics.tokens: Sum every billed attempt's input and output tokens, including retries and unsuccessful earlier rounds. Report per-round records and total tokens for each repetition. Report the median and range across successful repetitions. If any attempt has unknown usage, exclude that success from token aggregates and report its count. Do not declare a token prediction held with missing usage.
metrics.diff: Final source versus original source using diff -U0; added plus removed physical lines. Count automatic and model edits together. Report the median among successful repetitions.
metrics.location: Use original-source 1-based inclusive fix-spans. Each removal maps to its original line. Each addition maps to the preceding original insertion boundary, clamped to line 1; replacement additions map to the last removed line. Preserve multiplicity. Report the share of successes touching every span and median changed-lines-in-span / all changed lines. Empty diffs have null ratios.
metrics.automatic: Total actual safe repairs applied, and passes before any model call. Safe warning repairs preserve behavior; do not present cleanup as a semantic repair.
metrics.predictions: The five decisions and tie/missing-data rules are frozen in predictions-2.md. Classes are reported separately, not treated as new independent populations.

retention: Keep output outside the repository during execution. Remove temporary native objects after scoring. Retain complete bounded transcripts and receipt. Split transcript archives below 10 MiB each; do not drop failed attempts to meet size limits. Scan uncompressed and compressed content for the actual key and sk-or- before Git.
